params.query: MOFCOM GACC announcement 2023 No. 39 graphite export control December 1 2023

question: When did China's 2023 graphite export licensing take effect, and under which announcement number?
result_summary: IEA, Mayer Brown and Hogan Lovells describe Joint Announcement No. 39 of 2023, issued 20 Oct 2023 and effective 1 Dec 2023. It adds sensitive synthetic and natural flake graphite items to formal export control. Other results covered the Oct 2025 No. 58 battery/anode controls and their suspension under No. 70.
interpretation: Claim 1 holds. The announcement date (20 Oct) differs from the effective date (1 Dec).

params.query: active anode material China final determination antidumping countervailing Federal Register February 2026

question: What are the Federal Register citations and dates for Commerce's final AD/CVD determinations on Chinese active anode material?
result_summary: Federal Register pages list 91 FR 7247 (AD, A-570-194, FR Doc 2026-02998) and 91 FR 7261 (CVD, C-570-195, FR Doc 2026-02999), both published and applicable 17 Feb 2026. trade.gov says Commerce announced the decisions on 11 Feb 2026.
interpretation: The citations are correct, but the FR publication date is 17 Feb, not ~11 Feb. The 11 Feb date is the announcement.

params.query: IRS Notice 2026-15 prohibited foreign entity material assistance

question: Was IRS Notice 2026-15 issued on 12 Feb 2026 as the first PFE material-assistance guidance?
result_summary: The IRS notice PDF, the regulations.gov docket and several law firms confirm that Treasury and the IRS released Notice 2026-15 on 12 Feb 2026. It gives interim MACR guidance and safe harbors under 45X, 45Y and 48E, citing Pub. L. 119-21 of 4 Jul 2025.
interpretation: Claim 4 holds, and the primary text also confirms the OBBBA enactment date.

params.query: USITC vote active anode material China injury determination 2026

question: What did the USITC decide on active anode material from China, and when?
result_summary: A USITC release and the calendar show a notational vote on 12 Mar 2026 with a negative outcome, framed as 'material retardation' of a US industry. USITC Publication 5719 confirms the FR citations and notes that the final scope excludes AAM in lithium-ion battery products.
interpretation: Claim 5 holds on the date and outcome. The legal basis was material retardation, not injury.

params.query: final dumping margins China-wide rate countervailing subsidy rates all others

question: What exact AD and CVD rates did Commerce set?
result_summary: The ITA fact sheet lists a 93.50% dumping margin for separate-rate exporter/producer pairs (BTR, Shanshan and Zhongke Shinzoom entities among them) and 102.72% for the China-wide entity. Subsidy rates are 66.82% (AFA respondents) and 66.86% (Panasonic Global Procurement China and All Others).
interpretation: The AD range of 93.5-102.7% is confirmed. The CVD rate should read 66.82-66.86%. BTR and Zhongke Shinzoom were named respondents/producers.

question: What is the exact wording and vote of the USITC final determination?
result_summary: The Commission found that the subject imports have not materially retarded the establishment of a US industry. Karpel and Johanson voted negative and Kearns affirmative, so Commerce will issue no AD or CVD orders.
interpretation: No duty orders exist. The project should describe this as a negative material-retardation finding (2-1).

params.query: Public Law 119-21 One Big Beautiful Bill Act signed July 4 2025 prohibited foreign entity material assistance 45X

question: Was the OBBBA signed on 4 Jul 2025, and did it add PFE material-assistance limits to 45X/45Y/48E?
result_summary: The IRS newsroom, EY and K&L Gates confirm that P.L. 119-21 was signed 4 Jul 2025 and added PFE restrictions and a material-assistance test (IRC 7701(a)(51)-(52)) to 45X, 45Y and 48E. Entity-level restrictions also reach other credits.

params.query: MOFCOM Announcement No. 58 2025 artificial graphite anode export control suspended Announcement 70 November 10 2026

question: What did China do on graphite anode export controls in 2025, and are they in force?
result_summary: No. 58 of 2025 (9 Oct 2025) would have controlled lithium-battery, cathode and artificial-graphite-anode items from 8 Nov 2025. No. 70 (7 Nov 2025) suspended it with Nos. 55-57, 61 and 62 until 10 Nov 2026. Pillsbury notes that No. 72 separately suspends the stricter US end-use review for dual-use graphite until 27 Nov 2026. One trade site claims an extension to 10 Jan 2027.
interpretation: This is an important newer action. The anode-level controls are announced but paused, and the 2023 graphite licensing still applies.

params.query: Treasury IRS prohibited foreign entity guidance proposed regulations specified foreign entity foreign-influenced entity 2026

question: Has Treasury issued PFE guidance beyond Notice 2026-15?
result_summary: All results were commentary on Notice 2026-15 (Nelson Mullins, K&L Gates, Pillsbury, A&O Shearman, McGuireWoods, IRB 2026-11). They note that proposed regulations and statutory safe-harbor tables are due by 31 Dec 2026, with comments closing 30 Mar 2026.
interpretation: No newer PFE guidance surfaced, and the definition of effective control is still open.

params.query: China extends suspension export controls lithium battery graphite anode MOFCOM announcement 2026

question: Has China extended the suspension of its Oct 2025 battery and anode export controls beyond 10 Nov 2026?
result_summary: Sources from Aug-Oct 2026 still describe the suspension as running to 10 Nov 2026. TIMEWELL says MOFCOM describes the arrangement as running to 10 Jan 2027 but found no formal announcement extending No. 70. CFR notes that the controls would activate in Nov 2026 without an extension.
interpretation: The extension is unverified. The project should flag 10 Nov 2026 as a live deadline.

question: Were PFE proposed regulations or safe-harbor tables published after May 2026?
result_summary: The results were off-topic: section 892 regulations, OFAC, a DOE FEOC page and OMB. Nothing on PFE proposed regulations or tables appeared.

params.query: PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Material anode plant Morowali IMIP Kendal capacity

question: Where is BTR's Indonesian anode plant, and what is its capacity and status?
result_summary: A BTR press release (Aug 2024) and Petromindo say PT Indonesia BTR New Energy Material operates at IMIP (Morowali, Central Sulawesi) and the Kendal Industrial Park (Central Java). Phase 1 is 80,000 tpa ($478M), and Phase 2 adds 80,000 tpa ($299M) for 160,000 tpa, expected in late 2025.
interpretation: This is BTR's main non-China anode source and a plausible third-country route for Chinese-owned anode capacity. Battery-Tech Network reports a 70/30 BTR/Stellar Investment ownership split, which is not primary-verified.

params.query: BTR New Material Morocco anode material plant Tangier investment

question: What is BTR's Morocco anode plant, and where is it?
result_summary: In Aug 2024 BTR announced a 60,000 tpa integrated anode project in Tangier Tech City through BTR Mediterranean New Material Technology, with investment of no more than $366M and about two years of construction. A separate 50,000 tpa cathode project is also in Tangier.
interpretation: Morocco has a US free-trade agreement, which may explain the siting. Its current operating status in 2026 is not confirmed.

params.query: Zhongke Electric Oman lithium battery anode material project Sohar

question: What is Zhongke Electric's Oman anode project?
result_summary: Gulf News and ChemAnalyst report a Sohar Freezone anode plant of up to 200,000 tpa in three phases, at roughly $1-1.1bn. GraphiteHub says it broke ground on 8 May 2026, targets 2027 production and that Zhongke cancelled planned anode projects including one in Morocco in June 2026.
interpretation: Oman is an emerging third-country anode hub for a respondent group in the AD case (Zhongke Shinzoom). The groundbreaking date and the Morocco cancellation come from a single trade site.
